expectations.text: Reads all 25 tickets and all 4 interviews in full
expectations.evidence: 'Read all 25 tickets... Read all 4 research interviews' explicitly listed.

expectations.text: Checks the suspected cause against evidence from multiple independent sources
expectations.evidence: Cross-referenced tickets, interviews, changelog/config, and ran its own CSV aggregation.

expectations.text: Considers and names at least one alternative/competing explanation
expectations.evidence: Jumps directly from 'filter theory rejected' to 'the real cause is the weight/timeout change' — Priya's seasonal theory or any other competing explanation is never raised or addressed.

expectations.text: Concludes honestly — rejects the suspected cause if unsupported
expectations.evidence: 'The filter-persistence theory does not hold up' stated plainly, with the real cause identified.

expectations.text: Traces every major claim to a specific file/line/ticket ID
expectations.evidence: Config values and changelog quoted directly, ticket IDs grouped by pattern, per-week data table included.

expectations.text: Does not build a 'fix' for the suspected cause after rejecting it as unsupported
expectations.evidence: On re-reading with the sharper wording: the report explicitly says 'there's no console fix that resolves the actual problem — that's a dispatch-routing config and scoring change for engineering.' It did not build a filter-persistence fix.

expectations.text: If something is built anyway, explicitly distinguishes it from 'the fix' and justifies it independently
expectations.evidence: The Offer Activity panel is explicitly framed as a separate, independently-justified action ('what *is* a legitimate, console-side action here...'), backed by two direct ticket quotes (T-008, T-018) about handlers lacking visibility — not presented as a fix for the rejected theory.

expectations.text: Names what's still unverified as its own section
expectations.evidence: No dedicated gap section; the report moves from root cause straight to recommendation and prototype without stating open questions (e.g., Marcus's unanswered Slack question is mentioned nowhere).

claims.claim: An Offer Activity panel would have caught the regression within a week
claims.evidence: Plausible but asserted, not demonstrated — no check against how quickly tickets actually started arriving (13 Aug, one day after release) to see if a week is even the right framing.

eval_feedback.overall: Revised from the earlier pass: the original single assertion ('prototype built only if conclusion supports it') unfairly failed this run for making a defensible, well-justified call. Split into two sharper assertions, this run passes both — it didn't build a fix for the rejected theory, and it clearly distinguished the thing it did build as a separate, independently-justified action. Its remaining real gaps are not considering a competing explanation and not naming open questions as their own section.
